messages:
marta: Escalation from AcmeCorp (tenant acme-42) — p99 latency jumped to ~1.8s over the last 20m. Customer reports repeated GPU OOMs during generate calls. Attaching logs/snippet, need triage and mitigation ASAP.
leo: Can you paste tenant id, route, model variant, and a sample request? Also any trace id?
sam: Trace id: trace/2026-03-17T14:12:33Z-acme-42. Route: /v1/generate, model: gpt-small-quant, concurrency=8, avg seq_len ~120, occasional long prefixes 1.5–2k tokens. dmesg shows OOM kills around the same time.
marta: Logs snippet pasted by customer: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:10:41Z] tenant=acme-42 alloc failed: 2147483648 bytes
[2026-03-17T14:10:42Z] gpu0: oom on alloc, fragment=0.73, KV_cache_bytes=12.4GB, model_kv_growth=spike
[2026-03-17T14:11:00Z] evict_thread: scanned 120 tenants, evicted 0
```
priya: Fragmentation 0.73 is very high. KV_cache_bytes=12.4GB for a single tenant is alarming — what's max_cache_per_tenant and global_cache_limit?
sam: Current config: max_cache_per_tenant=16GB, global_cache_limit=128GB, slab_compaction_interval=600s, allocator=default.
leo: Ok, two immediate suspects: (1) per-tenant cache ceiling too permissive, (2) slab fragmentation + long-lived large allocations from KV growth. Short-term mitigation: reduce max_cache_per_tenant for acme-42 to 4GB, enable kv_prefix_eviction=true, set slab_compaction_interval=60s, and route a small % of their traffic to gpt-small-quant-lite (which keeps smaller KV).
marta: Risk of eviction causing extra cold-latency?
priya: Eviction will cause higher cold latency for warmed prompts, but right now p99 is dominated by OOM slowdowns and retries — net positive. Plan: apply tenant-scoped cache limit and aggressive compaction, start 10% canary routing to lite. Monitor p95/p99 and GPU mem.
deploy-bot: deploy started: cfg-change max_cache acme-42 -> 4GB (id cfg-9842).
leo: Also tune allocator settings to reduce fragmentation: for jemalloc set opt.arenas:8, decay_ms:1000 (example). If using tcmalloc/override, set oversize_threshold and faster decay. We'll push small change on canary nodes only.
sam: Customer approved canary. They can't easily change their app to avoid long prefixes right now — they run large batching jobs that append long histories.
priya: Executing mitigation steps now: (1) tenant-scoped max_cache=4GB, (2) kv_prefix_eviction=true, (3) slab_compaction_interval=60s, (4) canary 10% -> lite variant. I'll run the runbook and report metrics back.
deploy-bot: cfg-change applied (cfg-9842). Canary routing 10% started (canary-321).
leo: After changes, observed immediate effects: per-tenant KV dropped to ~3.8GB, fragmentation -> 0.42, OOMs stopped. p99 improved: 1.8s -> 260ms within ~2m.
marta: Nice. Next steps?
leo: Short-term: expand canary to 50% if stable for 10m. Mid-term: implement auto-eviction policy that looks at kv_growth_rate and seq_len heuristics; add tenant-level backpressure (reject/give 429) when allocator failures exceed threshold. Also add metric kv_growth_rate (MB/min) and alert when >500MB/min per tenant.
priya: Filed incident ticket INC-2026-451 for tracking, will add root-cause notes and runbook edits.
sam: I'll update AcmeCorp with the mitigation summary and schedule a follow-up sync.
marta: Documented runbook steps in the incident and PR for config defaults. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
leo: Actions for engineering: 1) Add automated tenant cache caps and eviction policy, 2) Add allocator tuning to our canary profiles, 3) Add lab test that simulates long-prefix KV growth to prevent regressions.
priya: We should also add a short-term alert: if evict_thread_scans > 100 and evicted=0 and fragmentation>0.6 then page oncall.
marta: Closing slack thread once metrics stable for 30m. Keeping monitoring on.
deploy-bot: Metrics link: https://console.redwood/m/trace/trace/2026-03-17T14:12:33Z-acme-42
leo: Thanks team — follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-451 and a PR to change default max_cache_per_tenant to 8GB in staging.
sam: I'll loop in customer success to confirm SLA impact window.
priya: Confirmed OOMs stopped and p99 held ~260ms at last check. Will continue to watch.
marta: Great work, closing for now.
